record.paper_title: The formation and evolution of early-type galaxies : solid results and open questions
record.context_brief: Viability of dry merging as a size-growth mechanism
record.original_question: How can major dissipationless, or dry, merging explain the gradual size increase of compact, superdense early-type galaxies at 1 < z < 2 while remaining consistent with the observed small-scale clustering of low-redshift early-type galaxies and the weak evolution of the high-mass end of their stellar mass function at 0 < z < 0.7? The question asks whether dry merging is viable as the main size-growth mechanism or whether other processes such as smooth envelope accretion or multiple frequent minor mergers are needed.

evidence.quote: The compact, superdense ETGs at 1 < z < 2 evolve by increasing gradually their sizes. A possible mechanism is major dissipationless ("dry") merging

However, it is unclear how the "dry" merging scenario can be reconciled with the properties of the small-scale clustering of low-z ETGs [73, 74] and with the weak evolution of the high–mass end of their stellar mass function at 0 < z < 0.7.
Other processes which may increase the sizes at z < 1 are the smooth envelope accretion [79] and multiple frequent minor mergers [10].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Compact, "superdense" massive early-type galaxies (ETGs) observed at redshifts 1 < z < 2 are known to be substantially smaller (by factors of a few in effective radius) than local ETGs of comparable stellar mass, and they appear to grow gradually in size toward the present epoch. Consider the following structural/cosmological constraints on the size-growth mechanism:

(i) the small-scale (sub-Mpc) two-point correlation function of low-redshift (z ≲ 0.1) early-type galaxies, which constrains the rate of close pairs and hence the frequency of major dissipationless mergers;
(ii) the weak evolution of the high-mass end (M_* ≳ 10^11 M_⊙) of the ETG stellar mass function over 0 < z < 0.7, which limits how much mass can be added to already massive ETGs by major merging without overproducing the abundance of very massive systems.

Within this setup, determine whether major dissipationless ("dry") mergers between comparable-mass spheroids can simultaneously:
(a) reproduce the observed mean increase of the effective radius R_e of massive ETGs from z ~ 2 to z ~ 0 (roughly a factor of 3–5 at fixed stellar mass),
(b) be consistent with constraint (i), and
(c) be consistent with constraint (ii).

If major dry merging alone is insufficient, quantify the relative contributions required from alternative mechanisms — in particular smooth accretion of low-density stellar envelopes, and a sequence of multiple minor (mass ratio ≲ 1:5) dry mergers — needed to account for the observed size evolution while remaining consistent with (i) and (ii).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent literature has converged on the view that major dry mergers alone cannot reproduce the observed size growth of compact massive ETGs while respecting clustering and high-mass-end stellar-mass-function constraints; multiple minor dry mergers (mass ratios 1:5–1:10 or smaller) are now widely regarded as the dominant size-growth channel, supplemented by smooth envelope accretion in some scenarios. Quantitative tensions remain (efficiency of minor mergers, observed minor-merger rates), so the question is partially rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Dry minor mergers and size evolution of high-z compact massive early-type galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: Sequential minor mergers of compact satellite galaxies are the most efficient at promoting size growth and decreasing velocity dispersion of compact massive ETGs.
status_evidence.claim: Minor dry mergers (not major) are the dominant size-growth mechanism for compact massive ETGs.

status_evidence.title: Can dry merging explain the size evolution of early-type galaxies?
status_evidence.snippet: Dry merging brings compact ETGs closer to observed correlations, but quantitatively the process is not efficient enough to fully explain the observed size evolution.
status_evidence.claim: Major dry merging alone is quantitatively insufficient to explain the observed size evolution.

status_evidence.title: The Effect of Many Minor Mergers on the Size Growth of Compact Quiescent Galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: Many minor mergers can produce the required size growth of compact quiescent galaxies.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple minor mergers can plausibly account for size growth at z<1.

status_evidence.title: Mass and size growth of early-type galaxies by dry mergers in cluster environments
status_evidence.snippet: Studies dry merger contributions to mass and size growth of ETGs in clusters.
status_evidence.claim: Cluster-scale studies support a mixed major+minor dry-merger picture for ETG growth.
